text: External examination of a chicken shows several visible parts. The comb is a red fleshy appendage on top of the head. Chickens have two eyes (one on each side of the head) that should be dark and prominent, and two ear lobes (one on each side). The beak has an upper and lower part and is usually a yellowy color. Two wattles (fleshy, generally red skin) hang below the beak. The breast, at the front of the bird, should be broad and plump. Wings carry a set of feathers on either side of the body that allow the bird to fly. Tail feathers are the same color as the rest of the plumage and point upwards. The vent is the opening through which birds excrete and through which females lay eggs. Chickens have four toes on each foot: three point forward and one faces back for balance. Ducks have webbed feet (three claw-like toes with flexible webbing between them), which help them swim more smoothly and faster by acting like a paddle.
